## Annotation

The release announces CSIL hourly-rate increases from 1 April 2011 ($27.63) through April 2013 ($29.50), estimates program funding rising from about $50 million (2010–11) to about $69 million (2013–14), and says more than 800 people then received CSIL (about 2% of home-support clients and 20% of home-support hours). It states that in December 2009 the Ministry of Health Services established a CSIL funding working group with the Association of CSIL Employers.

It also says new eligibility criteria would focus the program on disabilities and high-intensity care needs, with current clients unaffected — consistent with the grandfathering sentence later seen in [HCC Policy Manual 4.C](hcc-policy-manual-csil.qmd).

Quoted speakers (de Jong, Louis, Kramer, Jones) are named on the release. Their praise of the program is not treated as historical evidence about 1993–95.

A “Learn More” URL `http://www.health.gov.bc.ca/hcc/csil.html` is given. A Wayback Machine redirect to a 22 October 2012 capture of that URL was observed; the capture body was not fully fetched.
